task: A failed VPN login was logged from 198.51.100.200. Does this look like a credential attack?
rationale: NOTE: this is the dataset's third 'hard' scenario, built via a different cross-referencing mechanism than the two domain cross-reference cases (no third IP-to-malicious-domain pairing exists in the seeded logs without inventing new data -- verified by checking every log detail against every malicious domain and CVE). The event_type alone (failed_login) superficially resembles the brute-force pattern seen elsewhere, but lookup_ip_reputation shows a long-clean history (malicious=false, score 3, first_seen 2020-09-01) at what geolocate_ip identifies as an internal corporate VPN gateway (Example Corp VPN, Denver, US); query_logs shows exactly one failed attempt that succeeded 8 seconds later (LOG-0021), plus a normal multi-hour VPN session (LOG-0022) -- a one-off typo, not an attack. Cross-referencing all three tools is what correctly clears it despite the alarming-looking event type.

task: 192.0.2.77 made one outbound connection to an unfamiliar domain, and one of our hosts downloaded an unsigned utility from an unlisted source around the same time. Is this a compromise?
rationale: lookup_ip_reputation shows an elevated-but-inconclusive score (44) with zero named flagging sources; query_logs shows only a single low-volume connection to cloudmetrics-stats.io (LOG-0035) and one unsigned-binary download from an unlisted source (LOG-0036); check_domain_reputation shows that domain is itself only 'suspicious' (malicious=false, score 52), not confirmed malicious. Neither side of the evidence clears or convicts it, so the honest call is to escalate for closer review rather than force a verdict.
